description: Phase 3 Bhojpuri reasoning finetuning: starts from the Phase 2 pretrained checkpoint, tokenizer/vocab fixed, finetunes on the synthetic comparative-reasoning QA set (8000 train examples, see finetune/data/). Loss is masked to answer tokens only. Lower learning_rate than pretraining since this is adapting an already-trained model to a narrow templated task, not learning language from scratch. num_epochs raised to 20 (full pass over all 8000 train examples per epoch) since val loss on the prior 5-epoch run bottomed out around epoch 1-2 then rose (overfitting on the templated data) -- finetune.py now selects checkpoint_best.pt (lowest val loss) for the final test-set accuracy, so extra epochs searching for a better minimum are free of the overfitting risk that motivated the original epoch count. batch_size dropped 16->4 (500->2000 steps/epoch): applied preemptively -- the equivalent Telugu run (batch_size=16, same class-weighted-loss fix) collapsed to predicting only EOS/non-answer tokens (0% on every question type, including yes/no, which genuine guessing would get ~50% on by chance) with checkpoint_best.pt locked at step 500/epoch 1, the very first validation point. Diagnosed as too few *optimizer steps* (not too little data) before the first checkpoint -- a local diagnostic of the same fix on the smaller low-parameter model only started recovering around step 1500-2000. Since Bhojpuri high-param's architecture (15.1M params) sits between the low-param (7.34M) and Telugu high-param (25.5M) sizes, the same fix is applied here before running rather than after hitting the same failure. Reasoning dataset size raised 10K->20K samples (8000->16000 train examples) since the model revisits the same train set num_epochs=20 times and test uses entirely disjoint entity names by design -- more unique (name,value) combinations reduces the risk of memorizing train-specific entities instead of learning the general compare-and-pick skill, and also raises steps/epoch (4000 at batch_size=4, up from 2000) which further helps the EOS-collapse-escape fix. learning_rate dropped 2e-05->5e-06: with the batch_size/data-size fixes above, total_steps grew to 80,000, which stretches the cosine LR schedule so it barely decays for a long time in absolute step terms (verified: at 2e-05 peak, LR was still 99.7% of peak at step 4000 -- end of epoch 1 -- and didnt reach even half its peak value until step ~53,350, roughly epoch 13 of 20). Empirically, checkpoint_best.pt got stuck at epoch 1 across the full 20-epoch run: the model quickly learned to answer every question with a yes/no-shaped token (the easiest, most frequent remaining answer class) and never recovered enough to learn the harder name-comparison/copy skill needed for the other 6 of 8 question types, which stayed at exactly 0% throughout. A 4x lower peak LR keeps the same schedule shape but reduces the absolute magnitude of updates during that long near-peak phase, aiming to avoid prematurely overfitting to the yes/no shortcut before the harder skill has a chance to develop.
